selectedCourses.name: Personal & Professional Development
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
selectedCourses.contribution: Mandatory first-year academic writing, research literacy, personal development and civic engagement.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. selectedCourses.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces financial accounting, management accounting and investment appraisal, including accounting's social role and accountability implications. Students record transactions, prepare and interpret financial statements, and analyze performance and financing. The course then examines costing, pricing, budgeting, organizational control and sustainable management accounting. Investment decisions are evaluated using accounting and discounted-cash-flow measures. A case study analyzes the misuse of an accounting principle and its financial-statement effects.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.
selectedCourses.contribution: Develops financial and management accounting, financial-statement analysis, costing, budgeting and investment appraisal through NPV, IRR and cost-of-capital analysis. This supplies actual corporate-finance decision tools as well as business context, without becoming specialist financial econometrics.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. selectedCourses.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. AI foundations and limitations lead into applications across enterprise functions and industries, labour-market change, productivity, innovation, market structure and inequality. Governance, corporate responsibility, regulation and future scenarios connect technological developments to institutional choices. Students analyze business cases and competing scholarly arguments, then investigate a country's AI readiness, workforce, regulation and industrial policy.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: This course includes a multi-faceted exploration of AI’s business, managerial, economic and related societal implications. Designed for students with a strong interest in AI, it requires no prior technical background.
selectedCourses.contribution: examines how AI changes business and economic decision-making, supplying an application context for data-science methods
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. Students study AI's capabilities and limits, applications across business functions and industries, and effects on labour markets, productivity, innovation and inequality. Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.

selectedCourses.name: Money, Banking & Finance
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines financial markets and institutions, including the pricing of bonds, stocks and derivatives, interest rates and their risk and term structure, commercial-bank balance sheets and performance, financial structure and regulation, banking fragility and financial crises, central banks, money creation and monetary policy. Students apply algebraic and graphical analysis to financial and monetary problems. In the Stanford Banking Game they manage a simulated bank, analyse performance in Excel dashboards, forecast financial statements, and make evidence-based decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk. A small research project extends a selected financial or monetary research article through additional literature, a case study or updated evidence.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: We study financial markets (stocks, bonds, derivatives) and financial institutions (commercial banks and central banks). We address such questions as: Can you outperform the stock market? Why are banks inherently fragile? What do central banks do? What causes financial crises? Throughout the semester, student teams participate in a business simulation, the Stanford Banking Game. Each team manages a virtual bank and tries to maximize its share price.
selectedCourses.contribution: Studies bonds, shares, derivatives, banking, risk and investment decisions through financial calculations and a securities simulation. It supplies substantial finance content, without assuming advanced stochastic asset-pricing theory.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Examines financial markets, commercial banks and central banks, including interest rates, financial regulation, financial crises and monetary policy. Students analyse financial problems and manage a simulated bank in the Stanford Banking Game, using Excel dashboards and financial forecasts to inform decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk.

selectedCourses.name: Introduction to Economics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces microeconomic principles and short-run macroeconomic analysis. The microeconomic component examines supply and demand, strategic interaction, consumer choice, production, costs and competitive markets. The macroeconomic component introduces output, unemployment and inflation, then relates goods and financial markets through the IS-LM model. Students use algebra and graphs to explain economic behaviour and apply models to economic issues.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides the introductory microeconomic and macroeconomic framework needed for quantitative economic applications

This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.

selectedCourses.name: International Macroeconomics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines short-, medium- and long-run macroeconomic dynamics and policy, including international dimensions. Students study goods, financial and labour markets, inflation and unemployment, economic growth, expectations and the open economy. IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models connect markets and policy effects. Algebraic and graphical analysis and interpretation of macroeconomic indicators support the evaluation of economic developments and fiscal and monetary policy.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops macroeconomic analysis of growth, inflation, policy, crises and international trade using economic data

selectedCourses.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Develops microeconomic theory through consumer behaviour, imperfectly competitive markets and economy-wide allocation. Students examine choice under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences and cognitive limitations, then monopoly, strategic behaviour and labour and capital markets. General equilibrium, efficiency, externalities and government complete the analysis. Algebraic problem-solving and graphical analysis are connected to the interpretation and evaluation of research papers.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops advanced microeconomic analysis of uncertainty, strategic behaviour, market structure, equilibrium and efficiency

selectedCourses.name: Public Economics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines government intervention through the efficiency and equity effects of public policy. Market failure, public goods and externalities provide foundations for studying public production, collective choice, spending and taxation. Health, education, welfare and social insurance illustrate expenditure and redistribution questions. Students apply economic models, interpret data and graphs, evaluate research and develop a research proposal and paper.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.
selectedCourses.contribution: uses theoretical models and empirical evidence to analyse market failure, taxation, redistribution and public policy
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.

selectedCourses.name: Econometrics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

selectedCourses.name: Behavioral Economics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

selectedCourses.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces entrepreneurship and core business functions through the development of a startup concept. Students use design thinking to discover customer needs, define a problem, generate and prototype solutions, and construct value propositions and business models. Marketing, finance, operations, human resources and funding inform a coherent business plan and investor pitch. Entrepreneurial cases and a startup simulation examine decision-making, early growth and business lifecycles, with attention to societal impact and sustainability.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.

selectedCourses.name: Research Methods & Statistics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Research Methods & Statistics gives you a strong foundation in how business management—and social and behavioral sciences—move from mere practices to true fields of scientific study. You’ll learn how to plan research logically, from designing studies to working with real data using experimental and survey techniques. You’ll also study descriptive and inferential statistics, with a brief intro to multivariate tools.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides foundational research design, statistics and empirical-analysis skills for later econometric work

selectedCourses.name: AI Ethics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines AI through ethical theory and psychological accounts of human behaviour and interaction. Ethical debates address fairness, privacy, responsibility, alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Psychological perspectives consider development, clinical care, social and organizational relationships, forensic applications and cognitive neuroscience. Students synthesize literature and apply ethical frameworks in an analytical psychology project and a research-grounded podcast, with a creative communication component.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Explores philosophical foundations and implications of AI. Examines the history of AI, ethical issues like interpretability, bias and alignment, debates about AI consciousness and implications for human nature.
selectedCourses.contribution: adds explicit ethical analysis of algorithmic systems, including fairness, accountability, privacy and responsibility

selectedCourses.name: Decision-making in AI
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Develops the mathematical foundations of intelligent-agent decisions under uncertainty. Probability and Bayesian networks support belief updating and inference, while temporal models address changing environments. Decision theory, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems connect uncertainty to policies and expected utility. Multi-agent decisions introduce strategic and collective interaction, and probabilistic programming provides a framework for expressing models. Students work through equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces planning techniques for AI systems in deterministic and non‑deterministic environments. Addresses uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and optimizing behaviour under constraints.
selectedCourses.contribution: Studies probability and Bayesian networks, temporal models, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability, bandits and multi-agent interaction. It contributes substantive decisions under uncertainty and discrete temporal modelling, not a general resource-planning or logistics course.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Decision-making in AI examines how intelligent agents make decisions under uncertainty. Students study probability, Bayesian networks, temporal models, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems. Multi-agent decisions and probabilistic programming extend the analysis, supported by equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.

selectedCourses.name: Logic & Discrete Mathematics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces formal logic, abstract mathematical reasoning and proof. Students analyze propositions and quantified statements, work with sets, Boolean algebra, functions and relations, and develop direct and indirect proofs. Induction and recursive definitions extend these tools to mathematical structures. The final component systematically models processes and games without chance and investigates the existence and construction of winning strategies.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Focuses on mathematics of decision‑making, covering topics in discrete mathematics such as logic, patterns and structures, with applications to computer science and algorithm construction.
selectedCourses.contribution: Develops propositional and predicate logic, sets, functions, proof, induction and recursion, followed by formal modelling of games without chance and winning strategies. It supports mathematical reasoning; a full combinatorics, graph or optimisation syllabus is not assumed.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Focuses on mathematics of decision‑making, covering topics in discrete mathematics such as logic, patterns and structures, with applications to computer science and algorithm construction.

selectedCourses.name: Optimization Methods in AI

Adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimization extend the toolkit. Laboratories and projects require algorithm tracing, implementation and evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Covers computational methods for search problems in complex and adversarial environments. Includes uninformed and informed search, local and global search, adversarial games and constraint satisfaction problems.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops search, constraint satisfaction and optimisation methods in discrete and continuous environments

selectedCourses.name: Ethics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Studies moral reasoning through historical and contemporary ethical theories and close philosophical reading. Utilitarianism, consequentialism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics lead into Nietzsche's genealogy, Murdoch's account of goodness and Nagel's treatments of value, perspective, death and meaning. Reflection and research essays require interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Explores theories of moral reasoning—virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism—and discusses moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. Applies theories to practical issues such as animal rights, privacy, future generations, war, punishment, disability and equality.
selectedCourses.contribution: Develops moral philosophy through close reading, comparison and evaluation of ethical arguments and independent essays. It supplies ethical-theory foundations; econometric research integrity and adviser–client knowledge asymmetry are not assumed topics.

selectedCourses.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Develops experimental-design knowledge and practical statistical analysis for health and behavioural research. Students choose, fit, diagnose and interpret multivariable models, comparing means, analyzing categorical outcomes and studying latent constructs. R, primarily through R Commander, supports repeated practical exercises; SPSS is an optional alternative. Data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions and hypotheses to appropriate models, assumption checks, substantive interpretation and APA reporting.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: The course is necessary for students who want to pursue master programs in psychology and adjacent disciplines, as well as research masters in the medical domain. It is highly recommended also for all those who want to be researchers in other domains. In addition to technical training, the course emphasizes clear academic communication. It will equip you with the skills necessary to apply advanced statistical techniques to real-world research problems. With a focus on practical application through case studies and data analysis projects, You will be able to choose the appropriate statistical model for various research scenarios and address common challenges in data interpretation.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides multivariate statistics, regression, factor analysis and related inference methods useful for complex empirical data
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Develops experimental-design knowledge and practical statistical analysis for health and behavioural research. Students choose, fit, diagnose and interpret multivariable models for group comparisons, categorical outcomes and latent constructs. R, primarily through R Commander, supports practical exercises; data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions to appropriate models, assumption checks and clear reporting.

conceptJudgments: Closest provides substantial actual mathematical calculus/linear algebra/probability and inference, regression econometrics, micro/macro/public economics, programming/algorithms, continuous/discrete optimisation and probabilistic decision models. These materially address defining mathematical/statistical economic modelling and operations research rather than merely generic quantitative skills. The specialist advanced econometrics/time-series, formal stochastic-process breadth, simulation sequence and required major research remain clear gaps. Their disclosure does not substitute for the actual defining subject content already present.

Data-science option changes five courses37.5EC: database modelling/querying, C++/Haskell construction, neural/deep models, AI ethics and business/economic AI applications replace numerical/advanced calculus, accounting, public economics and general ethics. Sustained computational learning, software and predictive modelling organise the difference, with economics/econometrics retained. Business AI is bounded application/governance context; time-series use in neural networks does not become econometric forecasting theory.

Finance option changes four courses30EC against closest: business/venture foundation, relational databases, securities/banking/risk and behavioural economic decisions replace proof/discrete logic, advanced algorithms, optimisation and reinforcement learning. Accounting actually supplies investment appraisal, alongside finance and economic choice. Mathematics, probability, econometrics and numerical work make this substantive quantitative-economic finance study, without specialist stochastic finance or merely career padding. Data science and finance differ by eight courses60EC.

Logistics candidate challenged against current full151-course reference: actual optimisation, flows, dynamic programming, stochastic decisions and algorithms; Entrepreneurship/International Business provide market-entry/governance/business-model inquiry, sustainability courses provide real environmental topics, Transnational Business Law covers transport transactions. None turns the assembled programme into a sustained distinct logistics/supply-chain inquiry. Computer network scheduling concerns computing systems, not assumed transport/inventory operations. A fourth logistics programme would reuse the accepted optimisation core with weak domain substitutions. Rejected on content, not unavailable planning coverage; three supported alternatives meet existing maximum/stopping rule.
implementationFinding: All32 selected courses retain meaningful direct/complementary contributions. No Excel changes or app changes. Current offerings require bounded moves in allthree programmes. Additional advisory preferences put introductory data/methods before learning, linear algebra before probability/numerics and algorithms before advanced algorithms; all advisory slacks zero. Full description-only evidence considered for Econometrics, Advanced Calculus, Reinforcement Learning and databases. Accounting investment appraisal receives full consideration; decision modelling, logic, numerical mathematics and mathematical gateway traces corrected to actual substance.

alignments.rationale: Both study limits, differentiation and integration. UCR adds dynamic modelling; the comparator puts more weight on formal proof and includes multivariable Lagrange methods.

Both continue calculus into advanced analysis and differential equations. UCR also covers multivariable and complex calculus; the comparator places explicit emphasis on rigorous definitions and proofs.
Both provide foundational statistical methods; UCR Research Methods & Statistics is broader and more applied than the comparator's dedicated introductory statistics course.
Both cover multivariate statistical analysis; UCR teaches it in a behavioural-science research context rather than an econometrics-specific context.
Both are introductory programming courses; UCR uses Python rather than the comparator's Java-focused implementation.

UCR studies local/global and first- and second-order optimisation, alongside search, constraints and discrete methods. This is a substantive partial relationship to nonlinear optimisation, with a broader AI setting.
Both concern advanced algorithmic solution methods for optimisation problems; UCR is broader than the comparator's dedicated combinatorial-optimisation course.

UCR studies discrete temporal probabilistic models and Markov decision processes. This is a partial relationship to stochastic-process modelling; continuous-time chains, queueing and Brownian motion remain differences.
Both develop object-oriented programming, inheritance and polymorphism. UCR uses C++ and Haskell and adds software design/testing; the comparator continues Java and its libraries.
UCR Introduction to Economics covers both micro- and macroeconomics; this row aligns it only with the comparator's introductory microeconomics component.
Both develop regression-based econometric estimation and empirical analysis; the comparator continues with additional econometrics courses beyond UCR's single dedicated course.
Both provide finance foundations and quantitative financial decision-making, though the UCR course is broader in banking and practical investment decisions.
Both develop academic writing, argumentation and presenting. UCR teaches introductory research literacy and civic engagement; the comparator trains communication of econometric work and LaTeX.

UCR supplies moral-philosophy foundations corresponding to the general ethics part. It does not cover the comparator’s specific econometric research-integrity and adviser–client knowledge-asymmetry cases.

Software Construction added as partial object-oriented/functional Programming relationship; temporal probabilistic/Markov decision models added as partial discrete Markov relationship, with continuous time/queues/Brownian gaps explicit. PPD moved from career preparation to actual academic writing/presenting; careercore1 and jobmarket1 left unmatched. Other primary partial relationships retained: linear algebra,multivariate and basic statistics,probability,advanced analysis,nonlinear/discrete optimisation,micro/macro,regression,finance and general moral-theory portion of Ethics. Mathematics’ proof breadth, unmatched methods/linear optimisation,full stochastic/simulation,math-economics,marketing,timeseries,major courses/seminar,thesis andopen space are not filled through generic tools.
